feet-pivot-velocity.reason: Animator.velocity at steps 5 and 17 of HumanA's clip, off by about 3e-4 relative in one component: the feet pivot residual every HumanA play of the probe already has (also on the keys recorded before the human stream controls); open, not caused by the job.

foot-ik-legs.reason: The Animator's own Foot IK after a job changed the pose: leg muscles off by up to 2.4e-3 on single steps (stream.ik, stream.ikPass, stream.bodyLocal). Consistent with amplified rounding of a nearly straight leg: moving the foot goals by one single-precision step changes Unbound's own result by the same amount on the same value (measured once); see the residual row in docs/COMPATIBILITY_GAPS.md. stream.bodyLocal step 17 (muscles 23 and 25, up to 5.7e-4): on macOS already off before, on Linux with the Mono float opt-in (UNBOUND_MONO_FLOATS=1), where game code's quaternion product setting the body rotation evaluates as the Editor's Mono does; with the opt-in off (the default) they match on Linux.

stance-drift.reason: After a job's ResetToStancePose on an Animator that root motion has moved from the origin, the Editor's stance values step with the distance: its final pose under Foot IK (hips, arms, legs) is off Unbound's in runs of updates (the read-back body up to 3.3e-3, 3e-5 of the character's height; a straight leg's twist muscle up to 1.5e-2 by update 28). At the origin the two agree (stream.stanceInPlace). What exactly produces the steps is not known; see the residual row in docs/COMPATIBILITY_GAPS.md.

readback-solve-straight-limbs.reason: A solve after the job read the pose back on the rig's root scaled by 100 (bone.rotateThenSolve, bone.solveTwice) works on the re-based skeleton, as the Editor's does: the body is displaced toward the root (bodyPosition z from -105.5 to -1.07 at step 0, alike in both) and the goals are out of reach, so the left arm is straight (forearm stretch muscle 1.06). The roll of a straight arm is one turn that the upper arm and forearm roll muscles (41, 43) split between them: Unbound's split is off the Editor's in steps of 1.8e-3 that cancel in their sum, with the upper arm's and hand's local rotations that follow. Consistent with amplified single-precision rounding: moving the goal by one single-precision step moves Unbound's own split by 5.4e-3 at step 16 (measured once); which steps differ depends on the host (macOS and Linux runs differ). The left foot's muscles 26 and 27 are off by up to 1.4e-3 on some steps, not traced further. The same solve before any read-back matches (bone.solve); see the residual row in docs/COMPATIBILITY_GAPS.md. Bounded instead of listed, so that a larger difference on any step fails: each of these muscles within 1e-2 (largest measured on macOS about 9.0e-3), the two roll muscles' sum within 1e-4 of the Editor's on every step (largest measured on macOS about 9.0e-5), and the upper arm's and hand's local rotations within 1e-2 per quaternion component (largest measured 3.7e-3); every other value keeps the comparator's tolerance.

humanoid-generic-crossfade-root-motion.reason: A cross-fade between a humanoid and a generic state of one controller with root motion (genericCut.fadeToGenericOn, fadeToHumanOn, from the fade's start): the Editor blends the humanoid body and root motion with the generic state's during the transition; Unbound takes the humanoid motion alone while a transition runs. Open (Q754): the blend of the two motions is not measured beyond these rows.
